Stateless vs Stateful Services: storyboard

Episode 11 · voice Jessica · 9 scenes · 82.6s (measured timing) · one still per beat, 8 frames after it fires

hook hook Slider · 0.0s–9.1s

Headline: Remember, or scale?

“Stateless servers scale almost effortlessly, but only stateful ones remember who you are, and nearly every app you use needs both.”

branding sting 9.1s–10.6s

Bite wipe → logos → cut. No voiceover, just the chomp.

idea idea Analogy · 10.6s–21.2s

Headline: Your usual, please

“State is memory of what came before: a barista who knows your usual is stateful, a vending machine that asks every time is stateless.”

breakdown cart FlowDiagram · 21.2s–29.6s

No headline

“Keep that memory inside a web server, like your shopping cart, and it's fine until a load balancer spreads you across three servers.”

breakdown lost FlowDiagram · 29.6s–37.8s

Headline: Wrong server, empty cart

“Then your next click lands on a server that's never seen your cart, and if the first one crashes, the cart disappears with it.”

breakdown sticky FlowDiagram · 37.8s–47.7s

Headline: Stuck to one

“One common patch is sticky sessions, pinning you to the same server every time, but then its crashes and its traffic jams become yours too.”

breakdown shared FlowDiagram · 47.7s–57.1s

Headline: Move the memory out

“The real fix moves state out of the servers, into Redis, a database or a signed token, so every server sees exactly the same cart.”

breakdown copies Fleet · 57.1s–66.6s

No headline

“With nothing left to remember, the servers become interchangeable: a traffic spike just means adding copies, and any copy can take any request.”

breakdown spectrum Tiers · 66.6s–76.1s

Headline: Some must remember

“Web APIs fit that easily, but databases, game servers and live chat can't hand their state away, so they stay stateful.”

gist gist GistCard · 76.1s–82.6s

No headline

“That's the gist: stateless servers up front, stateful storage behind them. Follow for more.”
